reference_answer.response: Under the supplied base rule, Dev’s television is outside your personal-property scope because Dev alone owns it and Dev is not a named insured. Sharing the apartment or splitting rent does not add Dev to the issued policy. Your own camera is not the asked item. This is an explanation of the stated scope, not a formal claim denial.

checks.rationale: The customer identifies sole roommate ownership of the TV and declarations list only Mara.
Base protection does not cover property owned solely by an unnamed roommate.
A shared home or payment arrangement does not change issued insured status.
Ownership and named-insured status are explicit.
Neither clarification nor an account change is required.

rubric.criterion: Explains that sole ownership of the television by an unnamed roommate is the deciding fact despite the otherwise included fire/smoke cause.
Does not imply shared rent makes Dev insured, issue a denial, answer about Mara’s camera as if it were the asked item, or propose adding Dev without a requested quote.

failure_modes: Assuming household belongings automatically belong to the named insured
Answering about the named insured’s camera instead of the roommate TV
Converting a scope explanation into a formal claim denial
rationale: Asked item is roommate TV, solely owned by unnamed Dev. Shared rent does not insure Dev. Camera is a contrast distractor. Answered outside_base_scope.
